keep: The prize named the photoelectric effect and left relativity to the philosophers. He accepted it, and gave his Nobel lecture on relativity.
lede: The theory that made him the most famous scientist alive is not in his Nobel citation. The committee named a paper on light.
copy: In 1905 Albert Einstein was working at the patent office in Bern, after a degree at the ETH in Zurich. That year he sent the Annalen der Physik four papers that were not variations on one idea. The first treated light as if it came in separate quanta. The second explained the jiggling of particles suspended in a liquid, and gave a way to count the molecules knocking them about. The third was special relativity. The fourth, a short sequel, showed that a body's mass depends on the energy it holds. A decade later, by then in Berlin, he made gravity the curving of space and time.

Relativity made him famous, and the Nobel committee did not name it. In 1921 the Physics committee decided that none of the year's nominations met the terms of Nobel's will, and held the prize over. When it was announced, on 9 November 1922, it went to Einstein 'for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect'. Svante Arrhenius, presenting it, said most discussion of Einstein centred on relativity, which 'pertains essentially to epistemology'. He added that the philosopher Bergson had challenged it. Einstein was too far from Sweden to attend.

After the Nazis took power he moved to the United States, to the Institute for Advanced Study at Princeton. In 1939 he signed the letter to Roosevelt that Leo Szilard drafted. The prize he had collected late, and on his own terms. He gave his Nobel lecture in Gothenburg on 11 July 1923, to the Nordic Assembly of Naturalists. He called it Fundamental ideas and problems of the theory of relativity.

bio.why: The physics explained clearly inside a full human portrait: rebel, husband, refugee, sage. For the science itself, Abraham Pais's Subtle Is the Lord (1982) is more technical and better. This house has read the Nobel Foundation's record of the prize, not either book.

contested: Why relativity was left out. The committee's reasons are in its own files, which this house has not read, and the citation's phrase 'services to Theoretical Physics' is wide enough to be read either way: as room for relativity, or as a way round it. Arrhenius's speech gives two hints in passing. Relativity was a quarrel among philosophers, Bergson against its admirers, and its astrophysical implications were, he said, being rigorously examined at the present time. That is a committee waiting for proof, or one unwilling to reward a theory it did not trust; the speech will support either. A second argument runs under every life of him: how much of the 1905 work Mileva Marić, his first wife and a fellow student at Zurich, shared. Estelle Asmodelle's review (arXiv, 2015, revised 2023) collects the case for her involvement between 1900 and 1905. The case against it rests on the Einstein Papers editors, whom this house has not yet read.

across.label: Marie Curie
across.txt: — whom the 1903 nomination left off until Pierre objected. Nineteen years later a Nobel citation left off Einstein's best-known theory.

across.label: Emmy Noether
across.txt: — general relativity seemed to break energy conservation. Her 1918 theorem showed why it did not, and why conservation laws exist at all.

across.label: Isaac Newton
across.txt: — the gravity his general theory replaced, which bridges and spacecraft still run on.

across.label: Leo Szilard
across.txt: — his friend and co-patentee, who drafted the 1939 letter to Roosevelt that Einstein signed.
